subject: Request: temporary multiplex handshake escape hatch for FinSight POC
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary multiplex handshake escape hatch for FinSight POC

Team — looping you in on an urgent ask from FinSight (POC starts next week). They’re seeing session resets when our SDK tries to reuse TLS connections during multiplexed streams. The behavior looks like a handshake mismatch after a sequence of rapid connect/disconnects from their load generator.

What they need: a short-term platform-side escape hatch we can enable for the POC that disables multiplex reuse and forces single-session handshake semantics for that customer (or a tenant flag). They want this as a temporary config while we debug root cause; timeline is ~1 week.

Attachments: finsight-mpx-log-snippet.txt (log with timestamps) and po-customer-nyc-arch.png (customer diagram).

Questions:
- Is a per-tenant runtime flag possible without a full release?
- If not, can we provide a documented client-side workaround for their SDK to avoid the handshake reuse while we investigate?

Marissa: FinSight is sensitive to delays; deal is on the line (FS-2027-0912). Appreciate your signal on priority.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 10:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary multiplex handshake escape hatch for FinSight POC

Thanks Jordan — I pulled the log snippet. Looks like an edge-case in our multiplex session pool where a partially closed socket gets returned to the pool and subsequent handshake attempts trigger a reset when a new stream tries to reuse it.

Short answers:
- We can add a tenant-scoped runtime flag that disables connection reuse, but it’s not trivial to expose without a config release (needs a config gating and a safe fallback). Estimated 3 business days for a controlled canary on a small pool.
- Workaround: we can provide an SDK recommendation to set connectionMaxIdle=0 and enable per-request connection negotiation (adds ~25-40ms p90). I can draft the exact flag names.

Risk: disabling reuse increases token-serving cost and latency slightly; we should set expectations with the customer. Also need an ops rollback plan in case the flag causes resource churn.

Action proposals:
1) Ship tenant flag (canary -> staged rollout) — ETA ~72 hours.
2) Provide an SDK snippet to FinSight for immediate POC (ASAP).
3) Instrument extra telemetry for the next 48 hours to validate (I can add a quick trace tag).

I’ll scope the PR and link it here once ready.

—Logan
Logan Wright
Principal Runtime Engineer

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary multiplex handshake escape hatch for FinSight POC

Appreciate the quick triage. FinSight will accept a small perf hit for the POC but needs the config in place before next Wednesday’s demo (06/30). Customer message: "If we can’t run reliably next week, we’ll delay the paid POC start."

Can we prioritize the tenant flag to a canary tomorrow? If it’s ready earlier, I’ll notify Anna and validate internal acceptance. Also please call out the exact SDK snippet so I can pass it to their engineers — minimize back-and-forth.

Deal impact: medium-high. If we move fast here and the POC looks good, the account opens up to enterprise expansion.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Sales Engineering

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 13:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary multiplex handshake escape hatch for FinSight POC

Update: scoped the change. Plan: add runtime config key runtime.mpx.disable_connection_reuse = true (tenant scope). Implementation: 1) config check on session checkout, 2) metric gating to limit canary to 5% of capacity, 3) a toggle in the Console under customer flags.

I’ll open a lightweight PR (MPX-421) now. ETA for canary deployment: 36 hours if infra approves. I will also attach the SDK workaround snippet:

--- SDK workaround (Java) ---
// force new TLS handshake per request
HttpClient client = HttpClient.newBuilder().connectTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(5)).executor(exec).build();
Request request = Request.newBuilder().url(url).header("Connection", "close").build();
// note: adds TLS overhead per call
--- end snippet ---

If product (Kimberly) agrees, I’ll also add the Console toggle UI change to the PR but mark it for follow-up (non-blocking).

—Logan

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 15:09:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary multiplex handshake escape hatch for FinSight POC

Thanks everyone — I support the tenant-scoped flag approach as a short-term mitigation. A couple product notes:

- We should limit the number of tenant flags we ship as stopgaps; include an expiration note and a ticket owner so we don’t accumulate cruft.
- Console toggle can be deferred (make it API-first); ops can flip via internal tooling for the POC.
- Please add a customer-visible note in the POC runbook describing expected perf delta and monitoring instructions (who to call if errors spike).

If the 36-hour canary is feasible, proceed. I’ll align with Legal/Contracts on a one-time SLA addendum if FinSight requests explicit uptime guarantees for next week (cc contracts?).

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Reyes <anna.reyes@finsight.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, contracts@finsight.ai
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 17:48:00 -0700
Subject: RE: POC connectivity — temporary config for multiplex TLS reuse

Anna — quick update following internal triage: we plan to enable a temporary per-tenant runtime flag to disable connection reuse for your POC. This will force a fresh TLS handshake per request and should prevent the session-reset behavior you observed. Expected perf impact: +25–40ms p90.

Timeline: canary deployment in ~36 hours; if everything looks good we’ll roll it to your tenant before the demo window. In the meantime, you can apply a client-side workaround by setting Connection: close (sample attached) to avoid waiting for the platform change.

Let me know if you want a short sync with Logan’s team tomorrow to walk through the telemetry and rollback plan.

Best —
Jordan
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
